incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited a flaw in Canvas Free-for-Teacher accounts, regained access after Instructure's initial 'containment,' and defaced login pages of ~330 institutions.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim 3.65 TB and 275M records across 8,809 school systems (usernames, emails, student IDs, messages); Instructure took Canvas offline during finals and ultimately paid the ransom, receiving digital confirmation of data destruction.

incidents.vector: Cl0p group gained initial access via a malicious email attachment in Sept 2020, dwelled until May 2022, then escalated using an unpatched ZeroLogon flaw and a domain admin account.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 633,887 customers and employees published on the dark web (4.1 TB including bank details and disability indicators); the UK ICO fined the company £963,900 ($1.3M) for missing detection for ~2 years and monitoring only 5% of its IT environment.

incidents.victim: Russian aerospace firms and drone operators
incidents.vector: 'HeartlessSoul' / 'Versatile Werewolf' used phishing, malvertising, fake aviation-software installers and a poisoned SourceForge project to deliver a JavaScript RAT, PowerShell scripts and LNK-shortcut exploits (ZDI-CAN-25373).
incidents.impact: Stole GIS shape files, terrain models, GPS data and proprietary mapping data from Russian government and industry — operationally valuable for targeting, logistics and infrastructure mapping.

incidents.vector: TeamPCP / UNC6780 targeted AI environments and ML software dependencies as an initial access vector, then pivoted from compromised AI software into broader networks.
incidents.impact: Google's GTIG reported the group used the foothold to deploy ransomware and extort downstream victims; the same report disclosed the first AI-developed zero-day (a 2FA-bypass for an open-source admin tool) that GTIG blocked before mass exploitation.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated buffer-overflow zero-day (CVE-2026-0300) in PAN-OS User-ID Captive Portal; attackers injected shellcode into nginx, deployed EarthWorm/ReverseSocks5 tunnels, used a SAML flood to flip HA to a second device and systematically destroyed logs.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation tracked as CL-STA-1132 achieved root RCE on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, enumerated Active Directory using firewall service-account credentials and maintained low-and-slow access via open-source tooling.

incidents.victim: DAEMON Tools users in Russia, Belarus and Thailand
incidents.industry: Software supply chain → government, scientific, manufacturing, retail
incidents.vector: Vendor (AVB Disc Soft) compromise inserted a backdoor into legitimately code-signed installers from at least April 8; first stage profiled the host and only a handful of high-value targets received the second-stage QUIC RAT.
incidents.impact: Several thousand machines backdoored worldwide; targeted secondary infections at government, scientific, manufacturing and retail organizations in Russia, Belarus and Thailand. Kaspersky reports the operation closely resembles prior Chinese supply-chain campaigns against Notepad++ and CCleaner.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Tracked as UAT-8302; gains initial access via zero-day/n-day exploits, then deploys a custom toolset including NetDraft (a .NET FinalDraft/SquidDoor variant), CloudSorcerer v3, VSHELL with SNOWLIGHT/SNOWRUST stagers and Draculoader.
incidents.impact: Long-term access to government networks since late 2024 (South America) and 2025 (southeastern Europe); extensive Active Directory reconnaissance, credential extraction and lateral movement using Impacket, the gogo scanner and other Chinese-language tooling.

incidents.attacker: China — financially motivated e-crime group (GoldenEyeDog / APT-Q-27 suspected)
incidents.vector: Posed as a customer and socially engineered DigiCert tech-support staff into running a malicious .SCR screensaver file; a misconfigured CrowdStrike EDR agent on one host left the intrusion undetected for nearly two weeks.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole 'initialization codes' from in-progress EV code-signing orders, obtaining 27 EV certificates that were used to sign Zhong Stealer malware delivered in cryptocurrency-theft campaigns; all 27 certificates have been revoked.
Attackers gained access to Trellix source code; the company says no changes were made to its products and has notified law enforcement (Trellix is one of Europol's closest partners).

incidents.vector: Large-scale DDoS against Ubuntu/Canonical domains and APIs.
incidents.impact: Users globally were unable to install or update Ubuntu for several days; the same group previously took down BlueSky and Mastodon.

incidents.vector: Compromised an admin account and reset the protocol's admin-action delay to zero, allowing malicious cross-chain transactions to execute instantly.
incidents.impact: Approximately $5 million in crypto assets stolen across multiple blockchain integrations.

incidents.victim: Embassy of Cuba in Washington, D.C.
incidents.vector: Compromised the embassy's Microsoft Exchange email server as part of a broader campaign that hit more than 5,000 Exchange servers in 2026.
incidents.impact: Stolen email inboxes of Cuban diplomats; reporting indicates the operation targeted intelligence on the U.S. naval blockade.

incidents.victim: CNAM — Moldova's National Health Insurance Agency
incidents.vector: Initial access vector undisclosed; Moldova's cyber agency said no ransom demand was made and did not exclude Russian involvement.
incidents.impact: Personal and financial data on nearly every adult in Moldova exfiltrated — including financial details of all private medical providers under the national insurance scheme; ~30% of the database was either stolen or had to be restored from backups. Disclosed amid renewed Russian military pressure on Moldova.

incidents.victim: cPanel/WHM hosts including Guam government websites
incidents.vector: Authentication-bypass zero-day CVE-2026-41940 in cPanel/WHM (affecting all versions after 11.40) allows unauthenticated RCE on shared-hosting control panels; mass-exploited within days of patch release.
incidents.impact: Shadowserver counted ~44,000 cPanel systems showing signs of compromise; thousands of sites defaced with fake $8,000 Bitcoin ransom notes, others were wiped or used to deploy cryptominers and DDoS malware. Guam government sites were taken offline. Australia's ACSC issued a critical alert.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion followed by listing on the World Leaks leak site.
incidents.impact: Internal data leaked included meeting notes showing content directors said they would 'contact Moscow' for help publishing anti-Ukraine content — exposing apparent Hungarian-Russian propaganda coordination. Mediaworks has sued at least one outlet that reported on the data.

incidents.vector: Threat actor compromised Brazilian DDoS-protection firm Huge Networks (via a January 2026 breach of its CEO's SSH keys), then used Huge's infrastructure to coordinate a Mirai-based botnet of TP-Link Archer AX21 routers (CVE-2023-1389) and misconfigured DNS reflectors.
incidents.impact: Sustained massive DDoS attacks targeting Brazilian network operators — the same ISPs Huge Networks was contracted to defend. Each Brazilian IP prefix was attacked in 10–60 second bursts with four parallel processes per host.

incidents.industry: Multi-sector (healthcare, financial services, professional services, technology)
incidents.vector: Multi-stage 'code of conduct' phishing campaign used polished compliance-themed lures, PDF attachments, multiple Cloudflare CAPTCHA gates and Paubox encryption branding to funnel users into an adversary-in-the-middle Microsoft sign-in page that proxied authentication and captured session tokens.
incidents.impact: Bypassed non-phishing-resistant MFA by stealing authentication tokens for immediate account takeover; campaign delivered in distinct waves over 45 hours and primarily targeted U.S. healthcare, financial and professional-services organizations.
